From the IV agent’s late-morning screen run (10:59). Rule: Bull options-flow bias, explode score ≥ 60, market odds of profit ≥ 60% (breakeven at or below today’s price), max gain ≥ 0.5× risk, both legs liquid; up to 5 by bias, $2,000 max loss each. Probabilities are the options market’s own odds, so expected payoff is about the cost: higher odds come with a smaller win. The most any spread can lose is its debit. ⚠ = earnings or a catalyst can land before expiry (more binary). Orders are entered by hand at the limit or better.
Only 1 of 1 candidates passed today. The rule is not loosened to reach 2; the rest are listed below with the reason they failed.

🎯 Bull call spreads

Act on 1 of 1: MET · $1,520 of $10,000

Top 15 Bull names by bias with an explode score of 60 or more. Strikes are searched on the first expiry 21–45 days out: only pairs where the market-implied odds of profit are at least 60% and the max gain is at least 0.5× the risk qualify (so the breakeven sits at or below today's price), and the best reward/risk wins, at a limit of mid rounded up to $0.05. Act-on rule (fixed, not tuned on results): both legs bid, each leg's spread under 50% of mid or $0.10 wide, open interest at least the order size, still Bull; up to 5 by bias (ties: higher P(profit)), $2,000 each. P(profit) and P(max) are the options market's own odds, so each spread's expected payoff is roughly its cost. Each is priced to finish with some profit at least half the time, but the loss when wrong (the whole debit) is bigger than the gain when right. Delayed quotes: re-check prices before entering. This is a screen, not advice. Orders are entered by hand.

Bias (−100 to +100) blends today's put/call volume (30%), put/call open interest (20%), 1σ skew (20%) and estimated net premium (30%). Bull at +25 or more, Bear at −25 or less, otherwise Base. Net premium counts a trade at or above mid as bought, which is an estimate: Yahoo shows only each contract's last print. Bear/Base/Bull prices come from the options' own implied distribution, using put IV for the downside and call IV for the upside. There is about a 16% chance of finishing below Bear, 50% inside Base, and 16% above Bull.
